messages:
emma: Heads-up — seeing NVLink link flaps on rack12-node7 starting ~12:03 UTC. GPUs 0/1 showing bursts of Xid 31 and kernel retries. Affected service: emb-encoder-prod (us-west2). Observed ~40% tail latency regressions.

sre-oncall: Ack. Any thermal spikes or fan chatter? Is this localized to the node or whole rack?

emma: Localized to node7 (the other nodes in rack12 look fine). Temps on GPU0 hit 92C, fans 100%. PCIe AER counters climbing. Quick snip from `dmesg` we pulled: 
```
[12:03:14] nvidia 0000:2b:00.0: NVLink link 1 DOWN
[12:03:15] nvidia 0000:2b:00.0: Xid (31) GPU exception on channel 0
[12:03:17] nvidia 0000:2c:00.0: NVLink link 0 FLAP
[12:03:20] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ID 000e
```

ben: That looks like a hardware-level NVLink/PCIe instability, possibly thermal cycling or a flaky NVLink bridge on the card. Recommend immediate drain of node and avoid job restarts there. I'll start the drain and collect hardware logs.

emma: +1. Please cordon and drain, and tag the node for RMA if flaps persist after graceful reboot.

ben: Running commands now: `kubectl cordon gpu-rack12-node7` then `kubectl drain gpu-rack12-node7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`. Posting nvlink stats (`nvidia-smi topo -m` and `nvidia-smi -q -d LINK` output) to the hardware ticket.

jihoon: Can you also capture `lspci -vvv` for the NVLink/PCIe device and collect `AER` counters from `root`? Example quick command: `grep . -n /sys/devices/*/aer_* || true` and `cat /sys/devices/pci0000:00/*/aer_*` — I can parse counters for patterning.

ben: Collected `lspci` and aer dump, attached to the thread (see infra-bot log). Sample: 
```
0000:2b:00.0 Ethernet controller: NVIDIA Corporation Device 1eb8
  Capabilities: [100] Advanced Error Reporting
  AER status: Correctable error(s) 14, Unrecoverable error(s) 0
```

raj: Two quick checks: 1) firmware/BIOS PCIe link parameters — verify `Max Payload Size` & `ASPM` aren't being forced by BIOS updates; 2) check if GPU firmware/PMU recently updated — sometimes NVLink firmware mismatch can cause sawtooth flaps under load. If hardware looks flaky, RMA.

maria: Noted. If we pull node7 out of rotation, us-west2 capacity tightness will increase. We may need to temporarily shift some lower-priority jobs to us-west1 dedicated pools — that has a ~12% cost uplift due to cross-region egress, but keeps SLOs. I'm preparing a quick cost/impact estimate.

infra-bot: Node gpu-rack12-node7 was cordoned by ben at 12:08 UTC. Drain started. Evicted 18 pods.

ben: Did a graceful reboot of the host after drain. Post-reboot NVLink still flapping within ~3 mins under stress test (run: `stress-ng --gpu 2 --timeout 60s`), Xid 31 recurred. I suspect intermittent NVLink bridge or card-level thermal contact failure.

emma: Given persistent flaps after reboot under stress, let's mark GPUs 0/1 on node7 as DO_NOT_SCHEDULE and open RMA with vendor. Emma -> I'll open RMA and attach logs. Ben -> please snapshot the node and label the hw for replacement. Jihoon -> can you coordinate with hardware team for physical inspection (thermal paste, slot reseat) before RMA if they're available onsite?

jihoon: On it. I can do a reseat and inspect thermal pads tomorrow morning (APAC onsite window). If reseat/thermals don't resolve, proceed RMA.

maria: Action noted on capacity. I'll spin up a transient capacity buffer in us-west1 and throttle noncritical batch jobs. ETA for buffer: ~25 min. Cost hit: estimated $2.4k/day if sustained.

raj: Also let's add an alert rule: if NVLink link-down events >3 in 10m for same device -> auto-tag node with `nvlink-flap` and schedule automatic drain/preferred fallback to dedicated pool. We can include AER correctable error rate threshold. Will draft PR for alerting rules.

emma: Good plan. Logging action items: 1) ben — hardware logs + label/do_not_schedule + attach stress logs; 2) emma — open RMA ticket and attach logs; 3) jihoon — onsite reseat/thermal check; 4) maria — capacity buffer & cost estimate; 5) raj — alert rule PR.

sre-oncall: Thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated with RMA ticket number and final disposition. If replacement is >48h, we'll need longer-term capacity plan. :thumbsup:
